Contact matrix implied by a HERMES population

Source: R/contact_hermes.R
contact_matrix_hermes.Rd

Computes the age-by-age contact matrix that HERMES effectively uses for transmission, from the household, school-class and workplace structure of a simulated population.

Usage

contact_matrix_hermes(
  demographic,
  params,
  age_breaks = default_age_breaks,
  age_labels = default_age_labels
)

Arguments

demographic

Data frame with age, hh_id, classroom_id and workplace_id (NA when not in school or work), e.g. ve_sim_waning$demographic.

params

HERMES parameter list with contact_prob_household, contact_prob_school, contact_prob_workplace and num_contacts_community_day, e.g. ve_sim_waning$params.

age_breaks, age_labels

Passed to cut() (left-closed intervals).

Value

A square numeric matrix with dimnames age_group (rows) and contact_age_group (columns).

Details

Each day, HERMES gives every infectious person \(i\) and susceptible person \(j\) a contact weight $$w_{ij} = c_\text{community} + c_\text{household} 1[\text{same household}] + c_\text{school} 1[\text{same class}] + c_\text{workplace} 1[\text{same workplace}],$$ with \(c_\text{community} = 1 - \exp(-k/N)\) for k community contacts per day, and infection probability transmission_prob \(\times w_{ij}\). This function returns \(C_{a'a} = \frac{1}{N_{a'}} \sum_{i \in a'} \sum_{j \in a, j \ne i} w_{ij}\), the mean daily weighted contacts a person in group \(a'\) has with group \(a\), in the same orientation as polymod_nl. It is reciprocal: \(N_{a'} C_{a'a} = N_a C_{aa'}\).

Averaging over each age group ignores clustering: a household member of a case is at much higher risk than the age-group average suggests.

Examples

cm <- contact_matrix_hermes(ve_sim_waning$demographic, ve_sim_waning$params)
round(cm, 2)
#>          contact_age_group
#> age_group  0-4  5-17 18-49 50-64  65+
#>     0-4   5.42  0.91  2.91  0.77 0.79
#>     5-17  0.28 10.42  2.85  0.83 0.79
#>     18-49 0.38  1.24  3.29  1.14 0.81
#>     50-64 0.21  0.73  2.29  1.67 0.88
#>     65+   0.21  0.68  1.60  0.87 1.40
